feature_request: Add rate limiting to the login endpoint
acceptance_criteria: When a valid user submits credentials, a correct login results in a 302 redirect to the home page with a Set-Cookie header containing the session token.
A single IP address making more than 10 login attempts within 1 minute receives a 429 Too Many Requests response for subsequent attempts until the 1‑minute window expires.
An unauthenticated user attempting to POST to /login without providing credentials receives a 400 Bad Request response with error message 'username and password are required'.
When rate limiting is triggered, the response body includes the JSON field {"retry_after":<seconds>} indicating how many seconds to wait before retrying.
plan: Reuse the existing `flaskbb/auth/views.py` login view to add simple IP-based rate limiting. Update the view to record timestamps of login attempts in Flask's application context and check counts before processing credentials. If over the limit, abort with 429 and a JSON body containing {"retry_after":<seconds>}. All other existing tests remain unaffected. No new files are introduced.
